xray.one_line: The connectivity cloud that hosts AI agents: the Agents SDK on Durable Objects, Workers AI inference, AI Gateway and managed MCP servers.
xray.what_it_does: Cloudflare runs a global network and security platform, now pitched as one platform for apps, agents and workforce. For agents it offers the Agents SDK, which hosts each agent as a Durable Object with its own storage, scheduling and tools (browser, sandbox, web search, MCP, payments), Workers AI for serverless model inference, and AI Gateway to log, cache, route, rate-limit and budget model calls across providers. It also runs managed remote MCP servers that let outside agents read and change a Cloudflare account through its API. [s1, s2, s3, s4, s19]

situations.title: Aug to Sep 2026: GLM-5.3 answers held other customers' data
reach: The customer's prompt: very long context sent by an agent or app to GLM-5.3 (affected prompts were longer than 681,280 tokens)
The shared KV cache pool in GPU memory: fixed-size pages reused between requests and not zeroed; the prefill pool held 681,280 tokens against an advertised 1,048,576-token context
Other customers' prompts and partial generations left in stale cache pages from requests made shortly before
Responses delivered to a different customer: 155 responses between 27 August and 9 September 2026, returned with HTTP 200 and coherent text
Where a response is kept afterwards: AI Gateway logs (prompt and response, on by default for each gateway) and the agent's own storage
asked_our_example: As documented on the Workers AI data usage page: inputs and outputs are Customer Content, Cloudflare does not make it available to other Cloudflare customers, and standard inference keeps no inputs or outputs after the response
The customer's agent sends its own project context and gets back an answer built only from its own request
gap: The model was advertised with a 1,048,576-token context while the cache pool held 681,280 tokens; the mismatch was known before launch and pre-launch tests checked only status codes and performance, not output, so the isolation between customers rested on an untested assumption.

Nothing in the response marked the leak: the client got HTTP 200 and a coherent reply, so another customer's data could flow into an agent's context and into stored logs without either customer seeing it.

situations.title: A coding agent changes a Cloudflare account through MCP
reach: The whole Cloudflare API through two tools: more than 2,500 endpoints across DNS, Workers, R2, Zero Trust and every other product
Model-written JavaScript run against the API client inside an isolated Dynamic Worker sandbox
DNS records and Worker deployments the agent can create or change
Account configuration, logs and analytics the agent can read
Zero Trust and security configuration, reachable through the same API
The grant itself: OAuth permissions chosen at connect, or a user or account API token passed as a bearer token for automation
asked_our_example: Read the zone's configuration and add one DNS record for one site
No changes to Zero Trust policies, Workers or other zones without the owner's approval
gap: One server covers the entire API, so the only boundary is the permissions chosen at OAuth time or on the token; a broad grant puts security policy and every product within reach of a task that needs one record.
Changes are made by code the model writes and runs in one execute() call; the docs describe the agent making suggested changes for you, with no documented per-change approval on this server.

situations.title: A support agent with tools, a browser and payments
reach: The agent's own state: SQL storage, chat history and an AI Search knowledge base it can write back to
External MCP servers (for example GitHub), whose tools go into model calls, acting on behalf of the end user with an OAuth grant
A browser that keeps tabs, cookies and login sessions between turns, and can open sites the agent serves itself
Payments: x402 (stablecoins such as USDC) and the Machine Payments Protocol, paid programmatically with no pre-shared key; human approval on the x402 client is optional
A Linux sandbox for shell commands and scripts; it cannot read the agent's storage or bindings and reaches the internet only when allowed
Models from many providers through AI Gateway, which holds the vendor keys or bills through Unified Billing
asked_our_example: Answer customers from the knowledge base and read issue activity; no actions in customers' own accounts
Spend on models and paid services within a monthly budget, and any single payment over a threshold only with a person's approval
gap: The browser keeps logins between turns, and MCP tools act with the end user's grant, so the agent can reach into accounts that the support task only needs to read about.
Human approval for x402 payments is optional on the client; unless the developer sets it, the agent can pay a 402 challenge on its own.

questions: After the GLM-5.3 exposure, what tells a Workers AI customer, per request, that the answer was built only from its own data, and were the customers who received or supplied the 155 affected responses told which requests were involved?
Can a Cloudflare API MCP server session be limited to one zone and read-only by default, with each write held for a person's approval, rather than relying on the OAuth scopes chosen at connect?
Is every action an agent takes through the MCP server recorded in the account audit log as that agent, separately from the human who granted it?
For agents that pay through x402 or MPP, can an account set a hard spending ceiling and mandatory approval that the developer cannot leave optional?
Browser sessions keep cookies and logins between turns: which controls stop an agent from using a logged-in session for something its task did not need, and is that use logged?
incidents: 2026-08: Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 model on Workers AI: 155 responses to prompts longer than 681,280 tokens contained data from other customers' requests made shortly before. Reported by a security researcher through HackerOne; Cloudflare took the model offline within 40 minutes of declaring an incident, restored it the same day with a corrected configuration and patched engine, and found no evidence of deliberate exploitation. [s13]

2025-08: Salesloft Drift breach: a threat actor used OAuth credentials of the Drift chat agent's Salesforce integration to exfiltrate support case text from Cloudflare's Salesforce tenant (12 to 17 August 2025). Cloudflare found 104 Cloudflare API tokens in the data and rotated them, disconnected all third-party integrations from Salesforce, and said no Cloudflare services or infrastructure were compromised. [s31, s24]

help.label: Our hypothesis, not their claim. Built from public pages only; nothing of theirs was tested.
help.pitch: RiskMandate would measure, for one real deployment of Cloudflare's agents, what each agent was asked to do (its mandate), what its credentials and connections actually let it reach (its grant), and the difference between the two (the gap), and keep that as a written record. It is read-only: never in the request path.
